criterion: open/run/stop/restart + Doctor/attach without dead controls; every health/usage/diagnose surface works E2E or named-fails; cost never fabricates dollars
section: All phase headers + overview paragraph + E4 / John-in-the-loop cross-refs
message: Headers are labeled `Phase 1 — Phase 0`, `Phase 2 — Phase 1`, … while body prose, E4, dependency rules, and the overview still say `Phase 0` / `Phase 1` / `Phases 0–2` without defining which numbering system is canonical. A future maintainer (or Foreman sub-agent) asked to “finish Phase 1 before surface waves” cannot tell whether that means Ground Truth, Capability Inventory, or Enabling Machinery. Wrong phase skip is exactly how Retry/Diagnose get wired without inventory transcripts, cost surfaces render without the Rollup Evidence Gate, and the end-to-end trace schema is applied after surfaces already shipped. Dual labels without a single authoritative ID map are not documentation style — they are an executable ambiguity that will reintroduce dead controls and fabricated dollars under the plan’s own dependency order.

criterion: dead control / silent zero / mislabelled empty avoided by evidence-before-wiring; S1 is the only NS declaration
section: Phase 2 — Phase 1 (Deferred); overview; Phase 4 — Phase 3
message: The plan states the wave list is **not final until Phase 1 completes** and that surface waves are written from inventory verdicts — but it never names the artifact, owner, freeze gate, or doc-trio update procedure for that re-write. A future Stage-2/Foreman maintainer therefore either (a) invents waves mid-run without a second approval, or (b) runs a plan that cannot yet list the work that implements Doctor, attach, cost, restart, preview, cadence. Invented waves absorb “build it” into surface work (the failure mode the inventory was supposed to prevent) or omit a control entirely so S1 is the first time anyone notices. “Waves after inventory” without a **named re-plan freeze** (who edits which file, what John signs, what becomes immutable) is not honest sequencing — it is an escape hatch back into ad-hoc scope, which the exit register does not even list as an exit.

criterion: John can open/run/stop/restart real work including Doctor diagnose — surfaces must ship, not only harnesses
section: Instrumentation budget — reduced-instrument path (E4)
message: E4 fires “if Phases 0–2 have not completed by the point at which surface work must start,” but that point is never a calendar date, wall-clock budget, wave index, or John-signed milestone. The draft correctly names instrumentation overrun as a **likely** failure that leaves Diagnose dead under an excellent conformance suite — then leaves the only mitigation (E4) without a falsifiable trigger a future orchestrator can evaluate. Without a concrete “surface work must start by X” predicate, E4 will either never fire (harness eats the build → dead controls) or fire by informal panic (load-bearing items quietly drop → silent zeros and unbound honesty claims). A future-maintainer rule that cannot be applied without reinterpreting “must start” is not a budget; it is prose.

criterion: real Anchor work referent; nothing ships to v1.1.x collaborators; cost never fabricates dollars
section: Phase 1 — Phase 0 (verification task triple; collaborator smoke; cost_state isolation)
message: The draft hard-blocks Wave 1 on a still-blank TASK-NAME / path / command / engines / John confirmation block; requires a “named v1.1.x collaborator” and check that are not named; and requires a plan-time cost_state ↔ branch-isolation resolution that is still a question. A future maintainer inheriting an “approved” Master Plan with those holes has no shared referent for “real work,” no collaborator isolation protocol to run after shared-artifact writes, and no written isolation answer before cost_state migration. The plan’s own words say unfilled verification fields make **every** acceptance criterion unfalsifiable — so leaving them blank in the draft under review means the honesty framework is not yet executable, only described. Approving incomplete plan-time facts is how later waves invent a task, skip collaborator smoke, or cosmetic-label cost under isolation pressure — all North-Star violations the exit register was written to prevent.

criterion: unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero; every health/usage/diagnose surface named-fails honestly; cost labelling never from numeric zero
section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (named-state vocabulary; cost_state; failure-state table; attach reason enum)
message: The plan invents at least three parallel state systems — shared UI vocabulary (`measured/pending/unknown/empty/zero/unmeasured/failed/unavailable/unclassified`), `cost_state` enum (`measured/subscription_covered/free_tier/unmeasured/measurement_failed`), and per-wave failure-state tables (attach reasons, Doctor depths, preview classifications) — and never defines ownership, mapping, or amendment rules between them. A future surface-wave author will mint local labels that “look distinct” while the shared primitive still says `unknown`, recreating mislabelled empties and ambiguous zeros the North Star forbids. Without a single registry (state id → allowed surfaces → required render string → which lint/harness covers it), the shared vocabulary is a suggestion, not a contract maintainers can enforce when tables grow mid-build via fault-induction.

criterion: no dead control; surfaces work E2E or fail with named state — not handler-bound theater
section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (end-to-end trace artifact schema); Phase 4 — Phase 3 (universal acceptance)
message: Load-bearing honesty rests on `external_observable` being a side effect **outside the process under test** (row / file / pid / network). Many North-Star surfaces (typed attach error UI, projects-collapsed preference, named disabled Diagnose under E1, preview “binary — download”) may have no durable external side effect beyond render. The plan does not say how those controls satisfy the schema without either (a) failing the validator forever, or (b) faking an “external” write that proves nothing about user-visible behavior. Future maintainers under gate pressure will invent process-local stand-ins or mark `capability_call` from direct handler tests — reopening the exact dead-control GREEN path the schema claims to close. Either define per-control allowed observable classes (including render-only with stricter UI proof) before waves, or the schema is overfitted to write-path controls and underfits the NS control set.

criterion: nothing wired until real capability exists; dead control forbidden
section: Phase 2 — Phase 1 (evidence expiry; post-change transcript replay)
message: Any commit touching a cited file:line invalidates inventory rows and blocks wave close until transcripts are re-captured. That is right for honesty, but the draft never specifies the re-capture producer after Phase 0 (John live vs replay fixture vs harness), nor how non-semantic edits (import sort, comment, adjacent function) are scoped so invalidation is not noise. Future maintainers will face chronic false invalidation and either stall surface waves (Diagnose never ships) or start closing waves against stale EXISTS rows “because the gate is too expensive” — which is how dead controls return after the inventory looked green. Name the re-proof command, artifact layout, and invalidation granularity (symbol/endpoint, not whole file) or the expiry rule will be bypassed in practice.

criterion: named user-visible states; S1 is sole NS declaration — not silent “ten criteria met”
section: Exit register; John-in-the-loop (E5); Phase 6 — Phase 5 status strings
message: E5 lets waves proceed with criteria permanently `not verified — awaiting John` / never GREEN, while terminal copy still allows `ten criteria met; North Star pending S1` (or with signed exits). A future status reader — human or tool — cannot tell whether “ten criteria met” means ten GREEN honesty criteria or ten waves closed with unknown surfaces still on screen. That collides with the exit register’s own ban on the unqualified phrase when exits exist, and with the North Star’s requirement that health/usage/diagnose either work E2E or show named failure. If E5-shipped `unknown` attach/Doctor is allowed into “criteria met,” maintainers will report proxy success while John still meets incomplete controls; if it is not allowed, the status grammar never says so. Define whether any never-GREEN criterion forbids the “ten criteria met” token entirely.

criterion: Steward conversational proof is S1, not a silent claim of this build
section: Phase 6 — Phase 5 — S1 Validation Session
message: S1 is the only gate authorized to declare the North Star met, yet the draft specifies free-traversal sampling without session duration, minimum surfaces exercised, verdict artifact schema, or positive pass criteria (only “findings” and four blocking classes). A future maintainer (or John on a busy day) cannot distinguish “S1 done, NS met,” “S1 done, NS not met,” and “S1 informal chat, status advanced anyway.” Without a required verdict record shape (`task-name`, `duration`, `surfaces hit`, `blocking findings[]`, `verdict: met|not_met`, signature, date), S1 becomes another escape hatch — either a rubber stamp (silent claim) or an endless reopen with no exit. The North Star’s S1 clause is structural only if pass/fail is as mechanical as a wave gate.

criterion: open/run/stop/restart without dead control; exactly one restart control per context (as success criteria state)
section: Success criteria (dead controls vs stop/summary/restart)
message: SC bullet 1 requires dead controls eliminated for “a single restart control”; SC bullet 5 requires **exactly one restart control per enumerated restart context** and explicitly rejects cross-context unification. A future wave author implementing “the restart control” will not know whether product-wide singularity or per-context singularity is the acceptance object — and may hide secondary restart affordances or leave duplicates in non-enumerated contexts. That is a dead-control / competing-control defect class the North Star names. Resolve the success criteria so SC-1’s restart clause defers to SC-5’s per-context rule (or vice versa) in one sentence a maintainer can test.

criterion: gates that prove E2E honesty — host-computed attestations, not agent claims
section: Phase 3 — Phase 2 (attestation mechanics); Phase 5 — Phase 4 (cross-check); overview standing rules
message: Honesty depends on “the orchestrator” computing attestation counts, re-running samples, and cross-checking commits — but no binary, script path, or Foreman hook is named. Future maintainers will substitute sub-agent self-reports (the exact failure mode I50 forbids) under time pressure. Name the host process that is allowed to write pass counts into EXECUTION-LOG, or the host-computed rule is non-operational.

criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach
section: The exit register; Phase 6 — S1 Validation Session
message: Steel-man the plan’s own acceptance system: exits are enumerated, signed, conjunction-scored; S1 alone may declare the North Star met; E6 is closed for the four violation classes. Even then the premise fails. The North Star is not only “no dead/silent/mislabelled/binary lies” — it is a **positive capability claim**: John **can** Doctor-diagnose and session-attach. E1 (`not available on this build`) is a legal signed exit that ships a named disabled control. S1’s build-blocking set is only the four **violation** classes (dead control, silent zero, mislabelled empty, raw-binary preview). A correctly labelled “Diagnose unavailable — reason” is **not** a dead control and does not trip E6’s closed complement. So the strongest reading still allows: signed E1 on Diagnose and/or attach → criteria closed with exits → free-traversal meets no four-class defect → S1 authorized to declare the North Star met while John **cannot** perform the actions the North Star names. The exit register does not close the escape chain on the positive half of the North Star; it formalizes gutting it. Fix required: either E1 on any control named in the North Star’s positive clause is an automatic NS-unmet (and S1 may not declare met), or E1 on those controls is forbidden without a North-Star amendment, not merely an exit row.

criterion: without meeting a dead control; every surface … either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Phase 2 — Capability Inventory & Rollup Evidence Gate; Phase 4 — Surface Waves
message: Steel-man the plan’s anti-dead-control premise: EXISTS only with a real transcript (curl/CLI/REPL), STUB always “build it,” wave acceptance requires a schema-validated end-to-end trace with `capability_call` and `external_observable`. The foundational premise still equates **“capability can be invoked out-of-band”** with **“the user-facing control is alive.”** A dead control in product terms is almost always a **path** failure: button bound to a no-op, wrong handler, swallowed promise, feature flag off in UI only, or a STUB that the REPL path never hits. A pasted CLI transcript of the “real” backend function does not observe the click path; the inventory can stamp EXISTS while the control remains dead. The later UI trace is supposed to catch that — but wave scoping, “wire it” classification, and dependency order are all driven by the inventory verdict **before** that trace exists. The steel-man therefore schedules wiring and GREEN-prep against the wrong evidence object. Required: EXISTS (or “wire it”) must be earned by a **control-path** transcript (same interaction the user performs), not by a side-channel invocation; side-channel proof may support “backend present” but must not authorize “wire it.”

criterion: stop, and restart real Anchor work … without meeting a dead control
section: Success criteria (SC-1 vs SC-5); Phase 4 — Restart waves
message: Steel-man SC-5 as intentional de-duplication inside each restart context, with unification explicitly out of scope. The plan still opens SC-1 with elimination of dead controls for “**a single restart control** — work or not shown,” then SC-5 requires “**exactly one restart control per enumerated restart context**” and multiple scope names (run/session/engine/workbench). Those are not the same premise. Under the stronger SC-5 reading, John can still meet several restart affordances across contexts; under the stronger SC-1 reading, more than one restart control anywhere is a criterion failure. The plan never reconciles which claim the North Star’s “restart” is evaluated against. A build can GREEN SC-5 by cleaning each context while SC-1’s “single restart control” is quietly reinterpreted — or fail SC-1 while claiming multi-context honesty. That is not a wording NIT: dead-control elimination for restart is unfalsifiable until the unit of “control” is one object. Required: one locked definition — global single control **or** per-context uniqueness — and SC-1 rewritten to match SC-5 (or the reverse) so “restart works or is not shown” has a single testable referent.

criterion: Doctor diagnose … either works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Phase 3 — End-to-end trace artifact schema; Phase 4 — Doctor wave
message: Steel-man the trace schema: a dead control is one that reaches a handler and makes no capability call / leaves no external side effect. For attach/stop/restart that is often right. For **Doctor diagnose** and several health surfaces, correct success is often **report-only**: credential_present, auth_round_trip result, or “no diagnostic available” — no row written, no file, no child process, no mandatory network write. Forcing a non-null `external_observable` (row/file/pid/request) either (a) invents fake side effects to satisfy the validator (theater the plan forbids), or (b) marks honest diagnose traces `invalid`/`dead`. The steel-man of “one universal liveness proof” therefore breaks the Doctor criterion it claims to protect. Required: per-control observable classes in the schema — including **read/report observables** (typed response body + depth label + forced-failure distinguishability) as first-class alternatives to mutation side effects — with the Doctor wave naming which class applies **before** work starts.

criterion: open, run, stop, and restart real Anchor work — including Doctor diagnose and session attach; Steward conversational proof is S1
section: Phase 1 — Ground Truth (verification task triple); Phase 6 — S1
message: Steel-man the triple as the shared referent that makes every criterion and S1 falsifiable: all fields filled, all three engines, duration long enough to stop mid-run and restart, every wave and S1 cite TASK-NAME. Even filled, **one** task is asked to be simultaneously long-running (stop/restart meaningful), multi-engine (Claude/Gemini/Grok), attach-bearing, and Doctor-bearing. Those are different runtime shapes; a single “exact command” rarely produces all of them without becoming an unspecified kitchen-sink whose failure modes cannot be attributed. Until the plan admits a **task set** (or explicit multi-step scenario with named sub-referents), “real Anchor work” remains one label over incompatible exercises — and S1 free-traversal against “the Phase 0 triple” can miss attach or Doctor while still “running the named task.” The blanks in the draft also leave the Master Plan under review **currently** unfalsifiable; Wave-1 hard-block does not make the draft’s claims evaluable **now**. Required: either a minimal task **set** covering open/run/stop/restart, attach, and per-engine diagnose, or an explicit multi-phase scenario protocol with separate acceptance hooks — not one underspecified command line.

criterion: John can open, run, stop, and restart … (surfaces actually built, not only harnessed)
section: Instrumentation budget; Likelihood register item 2
message: Steel-man the budget: load-bearing vs discretionary named; E4 pre-defined with lighter forms; Phase 0–2 output capped; likelihood #2 mitigated by E4. The premise still has **no operational tripwire**. “If Phases 0–2 have not completed by the point at which surface work must start” never defines that point (calendar, wave-count, hours, or “first surface wave may not slip past N”). Without a numeric or calendar gate, E4 is only taken when someone notices overrun — the exact failure mode the section says is more likely than lying controls. Load-bearing items alone (vocabulary, tri-state harness, trace schema, cost_state, zero-inference lint) can still consume the effort. The North Star fails equally if Diagnose remains dead under an excellent harness. Required: a pre-committed surface-start deadline or max Phase 0–2 wave/time budget that **forces** the E4 register row, not a judgment call mid-stall.

criterion: without meeting a dead control (and Doctor/attach work end-to-end)
section: Phase 2 — three-way reclassification; Deferred build-it waves
message: Steel-man the anti-escape rule: STUB may never become E1; STUB is always “build it” or renegotiation — correctly blocks laundering dead controls into labels. The premise of the effort is still **defect-remediation on v1.2**, not open-ended backend construction. If inventory returns multiple STUBs on NS-named controls, the plan obligates new full capability builds (own waves, own acceptance, dependency order) with no cap, no sizing gate, and no pre-agreed “renegotiate North Star vs absorb N build-it waves” threshold. Until those waves GREEN, the user-facing STUB **is** the dead control the North Star forbids. Steel-man therefore creates either unbounded scope explosion or a long window where dead controls remain live in the product while “build it” queues. Required: inventory-driven **scope freeze** with John after Phase 1 — explicit choose per STUB: fund build-it in this effort (sized), amend North Star, or HALT — not an automatic infinite “build it, always” that the defect-remediation premise cannot carry.

criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; every surface that claims … usage … works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state
section: Success criteria SC-3; Phase 0 rollup spot-check; Phase 3 cost_state migration; Phase 4 usage wave
message: Steel-man the cost rules: E2 banned for dollars; wrong spot-check → `measurement_failed`; labelling only from `cost_state`; existing rows default `unmeasured`; no `$0.00` as fact. That prevents fabrication. It also permits a GREEN “cost honesty” outcome where **no surface ever shows a real dollar figure** — historical rows unmeasured, backfill deferred, measurement_failed or unmeasured as the steady state — while SC-3’s practical-usefulness clause (real numbers within 60s after the named task) is satisfied only for usage/time or waived via pending/E5. “Cost never fabricates dollars” is then met by **never claiming cost**, which is weaker than a surface that “claims … usage” honesty implies for cost chrome that still occupies UI. The steel-man of non-fabrication becomes empty chrome that looks like a cost surface. Required: define when a cost surface must show `measured` dollars vs when the control must be **not shown** (SC-1 style) rather than left up as perpetual unmeasured/failed; perpetual unmeasured on a surface that still claims “cost” is a mislabelled empty/unknown risk relative to user expectation.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Phase 1 shared-artifact ledger; Phase 3 cost_state migration
message: Steel-man the isolation design: per-artifact yes/no, named mechanism (separate DB, additive migration behind flag default off, versioned assets), collaborator smoke after shared writes. “Ships” is never defined. An additive nullable `cost_state` column on a **shared** database is still a schema change collaborators’ stack loads, migrates, or fails on — even if the feature flag defaults off and UI is v1.2-only. Flag-off does not mean “nothing shipped” if migration runs on shared storage. The ledger can record “isolation = feature flag” while the North Star’s collaborator clause is already violated at the schema layer. Required: define “ships” (binary deploy, schema migrate, shared config, package version) and ban shared-schema mutations unless the ledger row names a mechanism that leaves v1.1.x **byte-identical** on disk/DB (e.g. separate DB or non-migrating side store) — flag-default-off alone is insufficient.

criterion: Steward conversational proof is a post-build validation session (S1), not a silent claim of this build
section: Exit register status string; standing rules; Phase 6
message: Steel-man the reporting rule: unqualified “ten criteria met” only with zero exits; otherwise “ten criteria met with N signed exits …; North Star pending S1.” The plan correctly withholds NS-met from automation. It still authorizes a triumphant **criteria-met** prefix as terminal build status before S1. That is not a silent NS claim, but it is a **proxy-success claim** that the plan’s own prose says is how teams stop early. Steel-man of S1-as-sole-NS-gate is weakened whenever status leads with “ten criteria met.” Prefer terminal status that cannot be skimmed as done — e.g. `build proxy complete; North Star pending S1` with no “criteria met” phrasing until S1 returns — so the steward clause cannot be socially satisfied by the proxy line alone.

criterion: surfaces work end-to-end on John’s real v1.2 environment (implied by “on branch v1.2” and transcript-from-real-environment rules)
section: John-in-the-loop scheduling; Phase 2 evidence-by-transcript
message: Steel-man capture-once-replay-many: after first capture, harness does not need John live; E5 covers non-hard-blocker waits. Live-John list is “exhaustive” and omits the **first** inventory/rollup transcript capture on his real environment — yet Phase 1 rules require those transcripts from his v1.2. Alternate producers are promised “where one exists” but not named for capability transcripts. If John is the bottleneck (likelihood #1), Phase 1 stalls without E5 on the inventory itself, or someone captures against a non-John environment and launders it as “John’s real v1.2.” Required: name alternate producer or E5/HALT policy for **initial** Phase 1 evidence capture explicitly; do not list live-John items as exhaustive while the phase’s load-bearing inputs are missing from the list.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Phase 0 (profile fixture); Phase 1 (transcripts); Phase 2 (trace schema / EXECUTION-LOG)
message: The plan deliberately captures and commits the exact materials that hold credentials—real v1.2 profile state including cookies and localStorage, capability transcripts from curl/CLI/REPL against a live environment, and end-to-end traces whose required fields include `capability_call` arguments plus network method/URL/response. It never defines a redaction policy, a secret-class inventory, a non-shared store for evidence, or a gate that fails if auth headers, API keys, session cookies, or bearer tokens appear in artifacts under the Foreman tree. Shared-artifact ledger rows cover DB/config/static/endpoints, not evidence blobs. Without fail-closed secret hygiene, wave commits and collaborator-visible paths can ship live auth material to v1.1.x collaborators—or leave “isolation” as a ledger story while secrets travel through the same git history the plan otherwise polices.

criterion: open/run/stop/restart including Doctor diagnose and session attach without a dead control; every health/usage/diagnose surface works end-to-end or fails with a named state
section: Phase 3/4 — Attach induced-fault set; Doctor forced-failure fixture
message: Acceptable faults include “revoked credential,” “wrong key,” and “bogus session ID” against John’s real v1.2 environment, but the plan never requires an isolated credential fixture, a pre-fault snapshot, or a post-fault restore attestation. A GREEN wave can permanently revoke or overwrite the live keystore, after which Diagnose and Attach become dead or stuck in auth-failure for all subsequent work and for S1—exactly the dead-control / broken-diagnose failure the North Star forbids. “Forced failure proves the diagnostic is real” without a restore contract is a security test that can destroy the product surface under test.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Phase 0 shared-artifact ledger; Phase 2 cost_state migration; Phase 3/4 per-wave shared-artifact checklist
message: Isolation is “named per artifact” and collaborator smoke runs only after a wave already reports a modified shared artifact. That is detect-after-write, not prevent-before-write. There is no hard gate that blocks the first migration, static deploy, or schema write when the ledger row’s isolation mechanism is unproven, STUB, or absent—and no fail-closed default if a feature flag is missing, inverted, or ignored by a code path. Feature-flagged-off for v1.1.x is stated as prose, not as a pre-flight proof that a v1.1.x process cannot see the new column, route, or asset. The North Star’s collaborator clause fails the first time a wave writes under a false isolation claim; a later smoke check cannot unship a shared DB change.

criterion: Doctor diagnose works end-to-end or fails with a named, user-visible state (not theater); nothing ships secrets/behavior to collaborators via shared surfaces
section: Phase 3/4 — typed banner→Doctor handoff payload
message: The handoff payload is required to carry “raw signal” (plus issue id, engine, timestamp) into Doctor with a test that it pre-selects the issue. The plan never bounds what “raw signal” may contain, never forbids embedding full auth errors, token fragments, env dumps, or command lines with secrets, and never requires redaction before render or persistence. A diagnose path that “works” by dumping credential material into UI, logs, or shared session storage is both a security defect and an honesty defect: the surface claims diagnosis while leaking the means of account takeover, and any shared storage of that payload can violate the collaborator isolation clause.

criterion: session attach without dead control; named failure states (unknown ≠ empty ≠ zero); Retry re-issues a viable action or explains why not
section: Phase 3/4 — Attach honesty / Retry viability
message: `unauthorized` appears in the reason enum and “revoked credential” is an induced fault, but acceptance never requires session-binding or authz checks: that Retry may not re-issue across principal boundaries, that unauthorized must not collapse into timeout/unknown_session (security-relevant misclassification), and that attach traces prove the capability refused the wrong identity rather than only returning a typed string. Without that, an attach/retry control can look honest in UI while being a security-dead or security-liar control—retrying under the wrong session, or classifying auth failure as a recoverable transport problem—undermining the attach honesty and dead-control clauses.

criterion: Cost never fabricates dollars; nothing ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Phase 0 cost_state ↔ branch-isolation; Phase 2 cost_state enum migration
message: The plan allows an additive nullable `cost_state` column with backfill defaulting to `unmeasured`, “feature-flagged off for v1.1.x,” and only asks plan-time whether the column is acceptable under isolation. It does not require a concrete negative test: a v1.1.x reader must not observe new columns/routes/labels, and a flag-off path must not render dollar figures from partial backfill. A migration that lands in a shared database with defaults of `unmeasured` while v1.1.x still infers labels from numeric zero either fabricates cost semantics for collaborators or ships schema they never consented to. Isolation resolution as a written opinion is not a security control.

criterion: File preview shows human-friendly documents; binary no longer dumps as text; no raw-binary preview
section: Phase 1 new-window renderer split; Phase 3/4 Preview wave content-classification
message: Classification is magic-byte + content-type + size ceiling, resolving to named states. There is no path-sandbox rule (open only under allowed roots), no denial of symlink/escape, and no policy for active content (macros, embedded scripts, PDF JS) when reusing “native browser viewer” or an in-repo conversion path. A path-escape or hostile document can force the shared preview path into undefined behavior—raw dump, empty mislabel, or crash that presents as a dead/broken control—or process files outside the user’s intended project. The North Star’s raw-binary and honest-preview criteria are incomplete without a fail-closed open boundary; size and magic bytes alone are not a security boundary.

criterion: Nothing in this effort ships to v1.1.x collaborators
section: Phase 0 collaborator smoke-check protocol; Phase 3/4 per-wave shared-artifact line
message: Smoke is defined as a named collaborator check after modification, logged in EXECUTION-LOG. That is useful detection, not prevention. Combined with Finding 3, the plan still lacks a pre-merge / pre-wave isolation proof and a HALT that forbids further waves until a failed collaborator check is rolled back or renegotiated. Relying on post-facto human smoke for a North Star hard constraint treats collaborator contamination as an audit finding rather than a ship-blocker at the moment of write.

criterion: Handoff hygiene / nothing ships unintended changes affecting collaborators; controlled write surface for the build
section: Phase 0 Foreman containment smoke run
message: The smoke test’s success criterion is that a stage2 cwd can edit a repo-root file. That proves the run can touch paths outside the planning directory—including shared manifests and assets the collaborator ledger cares about—yet the plan does not require a subsequent write-allowlist or path policy for product waves. Security of the build harness is left at “containment works or we move cwd,” which expands blast radius for accidental shared-artifact writes rather than narrowing it. This is a refinement of isolation/hygiene, not a general multi-tenant hardening ask.
